clue.text: Intrusive ads showing dad dancing, maybe, with son

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
up means on one's feet and active, as when out on the floor dancing
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Online adverts that show a father embarrassing himself on the dance floor alongside his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dad dancing' is a fixed phrase for awkward middle-aged moves, but the two words work apart; being up means being on one's feet, as dancers are.
explanation.definitionFit: Web adverts that spring open in a new window over the page are a familiar nuisance of browsing.

clue.text: Preserved in aspic, as some modern master

indicators.note: something preserved in aspic is set inside jelly, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Some old-fashioned artist set in jelly like a museum piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserved in aspic' is an idiom for being stuck in the past, but here the letters are simply held inside 'aspic, as some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter was a leading figure of twentieth-century art, a master of the modern movement.

clue.text: Gather it's petition time

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or appeal

explanation.surface: Assemble, because the moment has come to present an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing a gather is a fold drawn into fabric, much like a fold pressed into a skirt.

clue.text: Pages split by plastic replica documents holder

indicators.note: the two letters for pages are prised apart by the other piece placed between them
plastic means mouldable, so the letters of replica are reshaped

explanation.surface: Pages divided by a plastic copy of an office device that keeps documents together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' reads as the material of the replica, but it is the anagram signal, giving APERCLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire clip is what holds a few sheets of paper together in an office.

clue.text: Hit parade captures heart of the one rejected by her stepson

indicators.note: the rearranged parade takes the central letter of the into its middle
hit in the sense of struck and battered, so the letters of parade are knocked into a new order
the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A chart-topping music show featuring a woman spurned by her husband's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit parade' looks like the pop chart; 'Hit' is the anagram signal turning PARADE into PAEDRA, which takes in H, the middle of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Theseus's wife fell in love with her stepson Hippolytus, who spurned her advances.

clue.text: Company "C" is in prime, which is dandy

indicators.note: the company letters and C sit inside the word for prime

parts.note: one's peak is one's prime, the best stage
the letter given as it stands in quotation marks

explanation.surface: A firm's C-grade unit is in its heyday, which seems splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, showy man who struts in fine clothes is likened to the bird with its spread tail, just like a fop.

clue.text: Guardian's sugar snaps

indicators.note: something that snaps breaks into pieces, so the letters of sugar are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sweets break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper; it is the definition, with 'snaps' signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hundred-eyed giant was set by Hera as a watchman over Io, an all-seeing protector.

clue.text: Who has lots of spirit, yet in dire trouble

indicators.note: the word for yet goes inside the rearranged letters
dire in trouble is dire put into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'

explanation.surface: Someone full of pluck who is nonetheless in a desperate fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dire trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'trouble' gives DIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky or gin maker keeps vats of spirits; the pun is on spirit as courage.

clue.text: A head of uncompleted major space project

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in poll tax

indicators.note: the word of loses its final letter, left unfinished

explanation.surface: A leader of an unfinished big programme exploring space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncompleted' seems to describe the project; it trims the F from 'of' to leave O.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's moon-landing programme of the 1960s and 70s was the largest crewed spaceflight venture of its era.

clue.text: Compact goods yard

parts.note: stock is the goods a shop holds

explanation.surface: A small, tidy depot where merchandise is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goods yard' is a railway depot, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact build is short and solid, the sense of thickset or chunky.

clue.text: Jazz star torn apart — she killed herself

parts.note: Cleo Laine was a celebrated British jazz singer

indicators.note: torn signals that the letters of apart are ripped and reassembled

explanation.surface: A jazz singer ripped to pieces, a woman who took her own life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn apart' reads as one phrase, but 'torn' is the anagram signal turning APART into PATRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen is said to have died by the bite of an asp after Antony's defeat, a suicide.

clue.text: Try to hold distinctive movement device

indicators.note: the word for try holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to try
an ism is a doctrine or distinctive school of thought

explanation.surface: Attempt to grasp a gadget that makes a characteristic motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gizmo is an informal word for a gadget or contraption whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Lecher acted like an MP with time reduced?

parts.note: an MP sits in Parliament, so sat is what one did

indicators.note: the word for time is cut down to its abbreviated form

parts.note: a year is a span of time

explanation.surface: A womaniser behaved like a politician while serving a shortened sentence?
explanation.walkthrough: YEAR shortened by 'reduced' is the familiar abbreviation YR.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat-legged woodland god of Greek myth is a byword for lust, hence a lustful man.

clue.text: Finch's wild statement

parts.note: wild meaning angry, as is cross
a bill is a statement of charges

explanation.surface: A finch makes an outrageous claim.
explanation.definitionFit: This finch has crossed mandible tips for prising seeds from conifer cones; it is one species of the family.

clue.text: Was too prone to apply veneer?

definitions.meaning: the past tense of overlie, to lie on top of something, as of smothering
to cover a surface with a thin layer

explanation.surface: Was the craftsman too inclined to add a finishing surface?
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' suggests inclined to, but means lying flat: overlie's past tense is the same word as the verb meaning to coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a covering over a surface is to coat it, and the past of overlie is to have lain on top.

clue.text: As a radical on the outside, Mo relaxed badly

definitions.text: As a radical on the outside

indicators.note: relaxed badly means loosened in a poor way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mo, an extremist at heart, chilled out poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' suggests an extremist, but in botany it means of the root.
explanation.definitionFit: The exodermis is a root's outer cell layer, so a root's outside is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Bike twisted round barrel, as might be found in well

definitions.text: as might be found in well

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the other piece
bike twisted out of shape has its letters rearranged

parts.note: BL is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A bicycle bent around a cask, the sort of junk dropped down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' gives KIBE; a kibble is a mining term, not everyday British.
explanation.definitionFit: A kibble is an iron bucket for hauling up from a shaft, such as in a mine or a well.

clue.text: Sulphur once providing lips with hue

parts.note: the brims of cups are their lips
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: An old yellow element that gave mouths their colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lips' suggests mouths, but means rims.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the archaic name for the yellow element, as in fire and brimstone.

clue.text: PC sort of old washer

definitions.meaning: a large boiler once used for laundry

explanation.surface: A police officer, a kind of antique laundry appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is slang for a police officer, and a laundry copper was a big metal tub for boiling clothes.

clue.text: Buzz gets permit for lock

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to ring them
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A phone call earns a licence to a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' looks like a fastening; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl or lock of hair is the same as a small twisted tress.

clue.text: Oscar's sort of thing: backing horse, herding swine

indicators.note: the reversed horse word gathers in the swine word as if rounding it up
backing means going backwards, so the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a pig is swine

explanation.surface: Oscar's kind of bet: on a horse while driving pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing horse' suggests betting, but 'backing' gives ERAM. Oscar is Oscar Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was famed for witty one-liners, a short clever saying.

clue.text: Is a donor complete, given love directions?

parts.note: to end is to complete
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
W and S are compass directions, west and south

explanation.surface: Has the donor finished, having received romantic guidance?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who donates funds to a college or charity makes a gift, as to fund a chair.

clue.text: Working to break demo ruler

indicators.note: the word for working splits the demo word open

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Labouring to disrupt a protest by a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A king or queen who reigns is a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Odd bit of canal that's turned?

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
a cut is a canal

explanation.surface: A curious stretch of waterway that has changed course?
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover piece of fabric or timber trimmed away is a remnant.

clue.text: Deodorised free-range hens feed across river

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the river letter, holding it
free-range means roaming loose, so the letters of hens and feed wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Smell removed after loose chickens eat on the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free-range' rearranges HENS and FEED to FESHENED, which spans R.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing a bad smell makes the air sweeter and cleaner.

clue.text: Common former leader

explanation.definitionFit: Heathland is open, scrubby land like a common, and Ted Heath was a Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: Sloth possibly inhaling argon gas

indicators.note: the sin word breathes in the argon symbol

parts.note: sloth is one of the seven deadly sins
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon

explanation.surface: A lazy animal breathing in an inert gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal; it is one of the deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarin is a deadly nerve agent, a toxic chemical weapon.

clue.text: Cyclist's condition?

definitions.meaning: a clause added as a proviso

explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist rides a bicycle, and an added proviso attached to a document is also called this.

clue.text: It appears here, chapter heading with bullets reversed

indicators.note: a heading is the top, so the first letter of chapter
the word for bullets is turned to run backwards

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition

explanation.surface: A chapter title with its bullet points flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the punctuation mark that follows 'here' in the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark right after the word is the item described, a self-referential definition.

clue.text: Truck, comparatively blue, carries weight

indicators.note: the outer word carries the other piece inside it

parts.note: blue means low in spirits, so more blue is more downcast
a load is a weight carried

explanation.surface: A sadder lorry carries a heavy burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatbed vehicle with a low deck for hauling heavy machinery is a kind of lorry.

clue.text: Lincoln's habit of putting everything into the other thing?

indicators.note: the word for everything is put inside the word for the other thing

parts.note: that, as opposed to this
all means everything

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln's custom of investing everything in something else?
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a custom; it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln famously wore a stovepipe topper, so it was his habitual garb.

clue.text: Want symbolic home to have entrance changed

indicators.note: the first letter of the home word is swapped for another

parts.note: the hearth is the fireside, the symbol of home

explanation.surface: Wanting a home emblem with a new doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of HEARTH becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, so it is want in the sense of need.
